bodies.linkedin:
In early modern Europe, the double-entry system was sometimes associated with theological and cosmological concepts, reflecting the symmetry of God's world and the scales of justice.

This methodology requires that every financial transaction be recorded using equal and opposite debit and credit entries. These entries ensure the books remain balanced by maintaining the accounting equation, where assets equal liabilities plus equity.

Luca Pacioli is frequently referred to as the father of accounting. He published a detailed account of this method in a 1494 textbook. Before this, the earliest known records utilizing the system in Europe were created by a merchant from Florence in the late 13th century.

Today, this model remains the only way to prepare accounts that fulfill the true and fair view requirement under Section 393 of the UK Companies Act 2006. It also serves as the fundamental requirement for creating financial statements that adhere to US GAAP and SEC mandates for public companies.

Financial records rely on these systematic checks to identify potential errors.
